answer: An operator leases one numbered beehive kiln on a tidal islet. Only that holder may glaze a unique bisque tile with a sealed underglaze pigment, press a fire-clay coupon stamped with a fable into the spyhole, and light the kiln while a published ebb leaves the causeway dry; they must stay until the returning tide cuts the road. Inspectors match tile serial, pigment batch, baked coupon, pyrometer tape, and causeway film. A shared kiln, leftover pigment, or off-ebb fire is one farm. N aliases cost N exclusive kilns, N unique tiles, and N live ebb-to-flood firings no single potter can stack.
